titulo: Stores aren't allowed to keep your card's security code 🔒
descripcion: Under the card industry's PCI DSS standard, merchants may not store card verification codes after authorization, even encrypted. Full breakdown in the linked video.

escenas.texto: Ever notice that some sites ask for the three digits on the back every single time?
It's because they're not allowed to keep it. Under the card industry's security rules, called PCI DSS, that code can't be stored after the purchase is approved.
Not even encrypted. Not even if you give them permission.
So if a store gets hacked, the code isn't sitting there to steal. Watch what happens when you pay, it's linked right here.
